content.text: Dashboard-displayed account and transaction values remain consistent with the corresponding state shown elsewhere in the application for the same records.

expected_answer.operand: every account or transaction value shown on the dashboard matches the corresponding value shown elsewhere in the application for the same record

content.text: A standard-user banking experience does not expose administrative-only capabilities or data.

expected_answer.operand: administrative-only capabilities or data in a standard-user banking experience

content.text: When authenticated as admin_user, the resulting banking experience includes administrative information or controls that are distinguishable from ordinary customer-facing banking information.

expected_answer.operand: administrative information or controls distinguishable from ordinary customer-facing banking information

content.text: When authenticated as frozen_user, transfer functionality is unavailable, disabled, or rejected through normal UI interaction.

expected_answer.operand: a transfer path that frozen_user can complete or bypass through normal UI interaction

content.text: When authenticated as error_user, a reachable loan-related banking view exposes the documented wrong-loan-total condition.

expected_answer.operand: a displayed loan total for error_user that conflicts with supporting loan data in the same view

content.text: When authenticated as error_user, the wrong-loan-total state remains distinguishable from a generic application or network failure state.

expected_answer.operand: a generic application-failure or network-failure presentation in place of the wrong-loan-total state for error_user

content.text: When authenticated as overdraft_user, the banking experience shows a negative balance.
A successful active-user login leads to the authenticated banking experience appropriate to the authenticated persona.

expected_answer.baseline: successful active-user login submitted from the Bank Demo login page
expected_answer.operand: authenticated banking experience appropriate to the authenticated persona

content.text: The authenticated banking overview reflects the authenticated user's persona and associated state.

expected_answer.operand: persona and associated state matching the authenticated user

content.text: Relevant accounts and balances are represented in the dashboard or reachable through the banking navigation.

expected_answer.operand: relevant accounts and balances on the dashboard or through banking navigation

content.text: Relevant transaction or activity information is represented or accessible where supported.

expected_answer.operand: relevant transaction or activity information on the dashboard or through supported navigation

content.text: When authenticated as slow_user, the product communicates loading or progress while the banking overview is still resolving.

expected_answer.operand: a user-understandable loading or progress indication during slow_user dashboard resolution

content.text: When authenticated as slow_user, the loading state resolves to an internally consistent banking experience.

expected_answer.baseline: slow_user banking experience is in a loading state
expected_answer.operand: resolved authenticated banking experience with internally consistent state

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied money because balances and transactions are financial state, auth because the dashboard is post-login, and user-reach because the dashboard is the authenticated overview every signed-in user depends on.
[risk_factors] Applied auth because this promise is a role restriction, and user-reach because exposing admin-only data to standard users affects every non-admin session.
[risk_factors] Applied auth because the promise depends on the admin persona after authentication, and user-reach because the role-aware experience is a primary dashboard behavior for administrators.
[risk_factors] Applied money because transfer access can change financial state, and auth because the restriction is persona-gated after login.
[risk_factors] Applied money because loan totals are financial values, and user-reach because the product explicitly documents this persona as a supported banking state.
[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the owner-facing distinction between an intentional persona state and a generic failure changes how the dashboard path is interpreted.
[risk_factors] Applied money because the promise is about balance display, and user-reach because overdraft_user is a documented supported persona.
[risk_factors] Applied auth because this is the post-login landing guarantee, and user-reach because the authenticated landing is the entry to all subsequent banking activity.
[risk_factors] Applied auth because the persona shown must match the authenticated user, and user-reach because misidentified persona/state distorts the whole dashboard experience.
[risk_factors] Applied money because accounts and balances are financial artifacts, and user-reach because account access is a core dashboard promise.
[risk_factors] Applied money because transaction/activity information is part of financial history, and user-reach because transaction visibility is core to the overview experience.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because a comprehensible loading state affects whether slow_user can use the dashboard at all, and change-frequency because loading indicators commonly regress when UI timing changes.
[risk_factors] Applied money because the resolved view contains financial state, and user-reach because inconsistent final state after loading undermines the main dashboard journey.
